News.title: How measles unleashed a wave of suffering in Bangladesh
News.content:
Delirious with lingering fever after contracting measles a fortnight ago, one-year-old Yusuf could soon die from a disease he should be protected against.

Propped up by his mother Nafisa on a temporary intensive care bed so she can keep the nebuliser over his mouth, the tiny boy is one of thousands of Bangladeshi children struck down by the worst global measles outbreak in years.

For now, an IV drip and oxygen sustain his fragile, listless frame. But Yusuf – whose eyes have been bandaged over to help him sleep – has a bleak prognosis.

The measles ward at the DNCC repurposed Covid-19 Hospital in Dhaka Credit : Simon Townsley/The Telegraph

It is, sadly, a common one in a country currently overwhelmed by measles.

An immunisation gap caused mainly by the overthrow of Bangladesh’s authoritarian government in 2024 provided the catalyst for an unprecedented surge in cases which has so far claimed at least 424 lives.

A tiny measles patient Credit : Simon Townsley/The Telegraph

More than 55,000 infections have been recorded since mid-March, according to the country’s Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), and hospital wards are over capacity with critically ill children.

Most of the victims of the epidemic are under 10, with the highest concentration among under-fives. Last week, 11 children died from measles in less than 24 hours.

Over the course of a week in Bangladesh, I witnessed the harrowing suffering unleashed when a whole nation’s vaccine distribution infrastructure is disrupted by bureaucratic collapse.

Six-month-old Mizanur Rahman on a measles overflow ward Credit : Simon Townsley/The Telegraph

For places where vaccine hesitancy has led to smaller recent outbreaks, including in London and Birmingham, it provides a blunt reminder of measles’ potential seriousness.

In Bangladesh, until recently praised by the World Health Organization (WHO) for its immunisation coverage, the mortality rate among children infected with the virus is high because of complications linked to malnourishment and pneumonia.

The ward in which I find Yusuf is in a former shopping mall converted into a makeshift hospital during the Covid-19 pandemic.

Rarely used since, except during a seasonal uptick in dengue fever cases, the Dhaka North City Corporation hospital is managed by the Bangladeshi military. It was repurposed for measles when the sprawling city’s Infectious Disease Hospital could no longer cope.

Eerily empty walkways between wards are lined with shuttered shop units.

Our escort, a uniformed army officer, tells me that in less than six weeks they have admitted more than 3,000 measles patients.

The DNCC Covid-19 Hospital, in a former shopping complex, has been repurposed to deal with the measles outbreak Credit : Simon Townsley/The Telegraph

“I was here during Covid and the dengue crisis in 2023,” says nurse Nazma Khan, 40. “This feels more severe because all of the patients are children. It is pitiful to see them in such a condition. They cannot express their suffering.”

As with many on the intensive care ward, Yusuf, from Shariatpur, three hours outside the capital, is not receiving the treatment he needs as medical fees are too expensive for his family.

“Doctors have told me that his brain has probably been affected by the measles infection,” says terrified Nafisa, 22. “Every time I turn away, he seems to get worse. He has been in a daze for so many days now. His eyes cannot focus anymore; he can’t really eat or sleep.

“He missed the measles vaccine, which he should have got when he was nine months old. Now he is so desperately ill. I feel helpless. The treatment he requires we can only get at a private clinic, but that would cost us twice what my husband earns in a whole month, for just a single day.”

Hospital wards are over capacity with critically ill children Credit : Simon Townsley

The disparity between the healthcare haves and have-nots is underlined by a flicker of movement that catches my eye next to Yusuf’s bed, a tiny cockroach scampering across the floor. On our way in, I was shown a dedicated private intensive care room for VIP patients.

At a nearby bed, exhausted parents Abdur Rajjak, 34, and wife Joynab, 33, are struggling to cope with having three of their four children, aged eight, five and one, in the hospital with measles. Their five-year-old, Obaidulah, is being kept separately in an isolation ward.

“All of my children missed their measles vaccinations,” admits Abdur. “I regret it so much. Normally, we would not be here. We are the most concerned about our son. He is in a very severe condition.

Paediatric Consultant Faria Yasmin examines an x-ray with a colleague on the Measles Intensive Care Ward Credit : Simon Townsley/The Telegraph

“Neither me nor my wife have really slept properly for ten days. It’s just the two of us. Our relatives are scared to come in because they don’t want to risk catching measles.”

As I walk around the ward, I am accosted by dozens of fearful parents. All seem equally shocked to be in this predicament so soon after what started out as a runny nose and high temperature.

It is noisy and chaotic. I quickly become inured to the unceasing background noise of rasping coughs, high-pitched wails and groans.

The highest concentration of measles patients is among the under-fives Credit : Simon Townsley/The Telegraph

One exhausted mother is asleep on a mattress that has briefly been vacated by a patient, before being rudely awakened for a new arrival.

Plastic bags stuffed with cough syrups and calamine lotion are scattered across the tiled floor. Some families eat rice and lentils from metal pots. Sanitation seems unavoidably ad-hoc.

Paediatric consultant Dr Faria Yasnim tells me there has been an “exponential increase” since children first arrived with measles rashes, the majority aged six to eight months.

“Usually, we would expect them to be protected by maternal antibodies passed on through breastfeeding,” she explains. “However, many of these babies’ mothers have also missed their vaccine, or they were too weak to breastfeed because of their poor diet. It is a scenario none of us have encountered before. Nearly all of the patients are critical and need oxygen.

“Often it is too late by the time they get here. The gap between infection and detection is too long.”

A mother lies next to her sick child on the measles intensive care ward Credit : Simon Townsley/The Telegraph

Bangladesh’s deadly measles outbreak this year is extreme, but several other countries have also experienced recent surges that run contrary to the overall global downward trend towards elimination through herd immunity.

Dozens of children have died from measles in Yemen, the majority unvaccinated. Last year there were 214 deaths from the disease in the war-ravaged country.

In Pakistan, 71 paediatric deaths due to measles were recorded in the first four months of 2026. Health authorities there say the spike is driven by a backlog of children who missed routine vaccinations during the Covid-19 pandemic.

Mexico is also undergoing an untimely acceleration in measles infection, which has triggered alarm ahead of the World Cup next month.

Dhaka’s population density makes it an ideal breeding ground for a highly contagious airborne virus spread by coughs and sneezes Credit : Simon Townsley

In the US, which is hosting the most games including all of England and Scotland’s group stage fixtures, WHO measles elimination status achieved 26 years ago is under threat from persistent outbreaks often triggered by anti-vaccine misinformation.

Eighty-five per cent of people infected in Utah this year had not received the standard two doses of the measles, mumps, rubella (MMR) vaccine.

A train passes through downtown Dhaka Credit : Simon Townsley/The Telegraph

Japan, granted measles elimination status in 2015, has also weathered a spike centred around Tokyo. Health authorities there suspect the virus might have been imported by foreign tourists.

Whereas the mortality rate from measles is approximately 1 in 5,000 in the UK, in Bangladesh there are around seven deaths for every 1,000 recorded cases during the ongoing outbreak.

Bangladesh is the only country in the world ranking in the top 10 for both population density and total population, making it ideal breeding ground for a highly contagious airborne virus spread by coughs and sneezes.

Until the uprising that toppled despotic former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, Bangladesh prided itself on its strong childhood vaccination programme.

According to the British Medical Journal (BMJ), the country maintained between 90 per cent and 95 per cent MMR coverage up to 2025, aside from an understandable dip during the Covid pandemic.

A defaced mural of Sheikh Hasina Wazed, Bangladesh’s reviled former Prime Minister, who is blamed for many of the current issues facing the country. Credit : Simon Townsley/The Telegraph

During the period of the interim government from August 2024 to February 2026, however, the mass measles vaccination campaign which normally happens every four years was missed. The last one was in 2020.

Stockpiles of vaccines became depleted as the procurement process slowed down and tens of thousands of health worker roles were left vacant.

Lacking foresight, the stand-in administration failed to react quickly enough to measles outbreaks in other countries in 2024. Another factor was that data from the private hospitals which many people in Dhaka use was not collated, the BMJ report found. It was the perfect storm.

Dhaka is perhaps better known for its dengue outbreaks Credit : Simon Townsley/The Telegraph

Mike Tildesley, Professor of Infectious Disease Modelling at the University of Warwick, said the difficulty facing nations with vaccination coverage problems is that the reproduction number for measles is extremely high.

As a result, herd immunity as defined by the WHO is only achieved when around 95 per cent have received the MMR jab.

“The consequence of this is that vaccination coverage doesn't need to fall very much for us to observe measles outbreaks again,” Professor Tildesley explained. “We've even seen this in the UK over the last few years, that measles cases have started to increase as a result of a drop in uptake of the MMR vaccine.”

A bus station in Dhaka Credit : Simon Townsley/The Telegraph

Bangladesh’s new government is now playing catch-up with an emergency nationwide vaccination drive underway. Over four million children have already been reached.

It is a race against the clock to prevent already weakened children from dying or suffering long-term complications, including inflammation of the brain and blindness.

At the Shishu Children’s Hospital in Dhaka, ICU staff on the hastily designated Measles ICU Ward have become accustomed to the grim spectacle of grieving parents carrying their tiny children’s bodies out, shrouded in white muslin cloth.

On one bed, garment factory worker Sheuli Akhter, 24, hugs her sleeping five-year-old niece Jammatal tightly, as if to shield her from encroaching danger.

Sheulii Akhter hugs her niece Jammatal in the measles intensive care ward Credit : Simon Townsley

The two gaunt, immobile babies on the beds behind are the worst cases I have seen. I struggle to imagine them lasting long.

In the southern town of Noakhali, serious cases are being treated in a disused office building next to the main government hospital. The emergency add-on space is over capacity, with gurneys lining the corridors.

Here, most measles patients are the children of smallholding farmers, fishermen, factory workers and labourers. Many arrived in the back of a rickshaw in their parents’ arms.

Nafiza Akhter watches over her seriously ill son, Yousuf Credit : Simon Townsley/The Telegraph

Their tiny throats strain with hoarse coughs, their eyes are unfocused, they are floppy, and their weakened bodies are covered with a rash that in many cases has also spread internally.

Crouching next to her prone five-month-old daughter, Maisha on another bed is 29-year-old Nazmum Nahar, her face etched by fatigue and worry.

“When we brought her here her body had turned blue,” explains Nazmum. “I thought she was going to die.”

Mohammed Akbar comforts his six-month-old son Abdul Credit : Simon Townsley/The Telegraph

Although slightly improved, Maisha remains at high risk. She is desperately underweight, having arrived at hospital in an already debilitated condition.

Her recovery has been inhibited by the fact that her own recent birth was not straightforward, resulting in a hefty hospital bill for a Caesarean delivery.

“We had to hand over all the money we had when she was born,” continues her mother. “That means we cannot even afford transport for her to be transferred to a better hospital.”

For some, the vaccination campaign backed by global vaccine alliance GAVI, UNICEF and the WHO has come too late.

Moyna Khanam lost her 18-month-old daughter, Jerin, to measles at the end of March. Jerin’s was one of the first registered deaths of the virus’s resurgence. She should have received her vaccine, but the local clinic was out of stock when her mother took her in last year.

Grief-stricken Moyna with her surviving daughter, Sara Credit : Simon Townsley/The Telegraph

Today, Moyna remains completely inconsolable, suffocated by raw grief. Her body shudders as she weeps, clutching her daughter’s favourite cuddly toy to her chest. Weeks have gone by, but she remains unable to process how her healthy, bubbly little girl was so swiftly snatched from her grasp.

I meet Moyna in the squalid, cobwebbed single room she lives in with her husband Tariqul Sabuj, 29, a plumber, and their elder daughter Sara, eight.

A photograph of Moyna Khanam with her 18-month-old daughter Jerin Credit : Simon Townsley/The Telegraph

Tariqul empties out a plastic bin liner containing all of Jerin’s clothing, shoes and scant toys. They sit together on the mattress in which they all sleep, sifting through mementoes of her cruelly short life.

Their cell-like concrete dwelling, which has two tiny, barred windows, is at the end of a dank, musty alley in a warren of decrepit housing blocks patrolled by stray dogs and rats. Sinks and toilets are shared between dozens of families. A hothouse for viruses.

Moyna is incandescent with rage as she berates the authorities she blames for Jerin’s awful death. Her words are muddled. She repeats the same phrase over and over like a mantra: “Why not me?”

Between stifled sobs, she musters the courage to explain her anguish. Tariqul is quietly resolute in the corner. Sara is mute and distracted.

Wasim Hawlader holds a picture of his 10-month-old son, who died after contracting measles Credit : Simon Townsley/The Telegraph

“Without Jerin this place feels completely empty,” Moyna admits. “I felt like she would be my companion for my whole life. We had such an emotional bond. She had so much energy, so much life to give.

“Now I just feel breathless all the time, like I am being crushed, and all that I can think about is the memory of when I was pregnant with her.”

“I refuse to accept she has left us,” she adds.

So many quiet tragedies are being absorbed into the frenetic chaos of Dhaka as the measles outbreak presses inexorably against its never-ending traffic.

Wasim and Ulfa at Mohammed’s grave with their surviving child Aysha Credit : Simon Townsley

Peculiarly for such a rowdy city, the cemetery in which 10-month-old Mohammed Yasin was buried at the end of March exists in an exclusive oasis of calm.

Amid rows of tiny mounds of red soil and stones already overgrown with weeds from recent heavy rainfall, I leave Mohammed’s numbed parents, father Wasim, 30, and mother Ulfa, 25, with their surviving child Aysha, three.

Freshly dug plots are the final resting place of infant measles patients.

In this beautiful, verdant spot, more like a public garden than a graveyard, sentry-still Ulfa prays silently, a potent symbol of the very real danger of neglecting the vaccine.

News.title: Guardiola’s imminent exit derails Man City despite fans’ cry for ‘one more year’
News.content:
Bournemouth are on a 16-match unbeaten run in the league, winning eight and drawing eight, which is the longest run of any side in the competition this season. The hosts come into this game in sixth, four points behind Liverpool in the final Champions League place. Bournemouth could go one point behind Liverpool going into the final game with a win but anything less than a win will probably end Bournemouth’s hope of a Champions League place, considering Liverpool’s superior goal difference. Both managers in the dugouts tonight appear to be in the final week of their tenures at their respective clubs as this will be Andoni Iraola’s final home game in charge of Bournemouth.

“It would be lovely for me,” said Iraola. “It would be the best way to finish these amazing three seasons. Especially this year, it has been really challenging for me as a coach because we have changed a lot the team and we have changed, not completely our style, but it is a different type of football comparing to last season. It would be the best way to end it. We are really close, but there is a big difference between being really close and getting it and grabbing it. We are in this moment where we have to do this final step. We have two chances but we want to do it tomorrow [tonight].”

When these sides met at the Etihad back in November, Manchester City won 3-1 thanks to goals from Nico O’Reilly and a double from Erling Haaland. The omens would appear to be on Manchester City’s side; they have won 16 of the 17 Premier League meetings between the sides, although Bournemouth’s only win in that span was in this fixture last season when they won 2-1.

News.title: ​Night of north London anguish as Spurs relegation fears go to final day
News.content:
Defeat again, the 17th of the season from hell, while 16 places above Arsenal claimed their seventh league title since Spurs won their last in 1961. The unbearable weight of all that history will have to be set aside for now because there is still a strong possibility that Spurs will be playing in the Football League next season. Their Premier League lives rest on them taking a point against Everton on Sunday – at their home stadium where they have won just twice all season.

Afterwards, their new manager Roberto De Zerbi made clear what was at stake – much more than when Spurs competed for their first trophy in 17 years in the Europa League final last season. “Now we play for something more important,” he said, directly referencing the final in Bilbao. “The history of the club and the dignity is more important than the trophy.” Spurs have a great deal more than just their dignity to lose with relegation, as any glance at their operating costs will indicate – but the point was well made.

They were beaten by Chelsea, a side that had not won any of their previous seven Premier League games – and now can no longer qualify for the Champions League. But the crisis for Spurs is on a different scale. The players, including the substitute James Maddison, left the pitch asking referee Stuart Attwell for more time. It is time that is running out. This result opened up for West Ham United a narrow shaft of light that, in spite of their own recent form, they may yet emerge from their own relegation death spiral.

News.title: Nasdaq plunges as US bond sell-off deepens
News.content:
Stocks fell sharply on Wall Street as inflation fears pushed up the cost of US government borrowing to its highest level since 2007.

The Nasdaq Composite sank by as much as 1.7pc as it was swept up in a global bond market sell-off driven by concerns over the war in the Middle East.

Tensions remain high over whether a peace deal can be reached between the US and Iran to end the conflict that has sent energy prices soaring.

Oil had fallen on Tuesday, with Brent crude down 1pc below $111 a barrel, after Donald Trump said he had held off launching a new offensive in hopes of striking a deal.

But Iran’s army has warned that it would “open new fronts” against the United States if it resumes attacks.

Concerns over an extended conflict, and higher energy prices, have steadily pushed up the cost of US government borrowing during the war.

The yield on 30-year US Treasury bonds – a guide to the interest rate it pays to borrow money – has climbed from 4.61pc at the end of February to nearly 5.2pc, the highest since 2007.

Steve Sosnick of Interactive Brokers said: “After pretending this was not a problem, I think (the market) has now decided that higher yields are in fact a problem.

“But we aren’t seeing panic or anything like that.”

It comes as Britain awaits official inflation figures on Wednesday that will show how the Iran war is affecting prices.

On Tuesday, petrol prices rose to their highest level since the start of the war, with a litre of unleaded costing 158.52p.

What happened overnight

Markets steadied overnight after Donald Trump said he had postponed planned strikes on Iran, raising hopes that a fresh diplomatic push could avert a wider Middle East conflict and further disruption to global oil supplies.

Oil prices fell back from earlier highs after the US president said Gulf allies, including Saudi Arabia and Qatar, had asked Washington to “hold off” military action while negotiations continued. The retreat in crude prices helped Wall Street pare losses and pushed Treasury yields lower.

Tokyo’s Nikkei 225 index was down 1.75pc at 58,475.90, dragged lower by technology stocks as investors worried about rising oil prices and higher global bond yields. South Korea’s Kospi was also weaker after recent record highs, with chipmakers under pressure ahead of key Nvidia earnings.

News.title: Uganda bans hugs and handshakes as two cases of Ebola are confirmed
News.content:
Uganda has banned handshakes and hugs after two cases of Ebola were confirmed in the country amid a major outbreak in the neighbouring Democratic Republic of Congo.

Dr Diana Atwine, Permanent Secretary at the Ministry of Health, on Tuesday urged the public to follow preventive measures including the temporary ban on handshakes, hugging and unnecessary physical contact.

“We are saying people must stop greeting… this [virus] relies upon physical contact,” she told a press conference.

Uganda’s health ministry has also advised the public to wash their hands with soap, use alcohol-based hand sanitisers and report any symptoms including fever, vomiting or bleeding immediately.

The two cases confirmed in Uganda are linked to the outbreak in the DRC, where 130 people have died and at least 500 people are believed to have been infected with the rare Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, for which there is no approved vaccine or treatment.

One of the cases, a 59-year-old man, died on Thursday, while the second patient remains under isolation and close monitoring, Ugandan health officials say.

Three countries in Southeast Asia have begun tightening their borders in response to the outbreak in recent days.

Thailand, Vietnam and Indonesia have all increased their surveillance of hospitals and airports, whilst watching border quarantine checkpoints closely.

Thailand’s Department of Disease Control (DDC) and Vietnam’s Ministry of Health have both issued guidance urging those returning from affected areas to monitor their health for symptoms of Ebola, while Indonesia’s health ministry has said that suspected cases will immediately be referred to designated hospitals.

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola breaks silence on Man City exit after draw against Bournemouth
Sports.content:
PEP GUARDIOLA didn’t confirm that he is leaving Manchester City at the end of the season.

The Sky Blues boss was quizzed again on his future following tonight’s 1-1 draw away to Bournemouth – a result that handed Arsenal their first title in 22 years.





That came just a day after reports emerged claiming he will leave the Etihad this summer.

While Guardiola insisted he still has one year left on his contract, he stopped short of giving any firm commitment beyond that.

Asked directly what the next chapter of his story would be at City, Guardiola said: “I would say that I have one more year of my contract, and the conversations I have many, many years – whatever you announce… during the competition is a bad result, and the first person I have to talk to is my Chairman.

“When the season is finished we will see, and afterwards we will take the decision.

“I have one more year on my contract, and I won’t tell you here because I have to talk with my Chairman, my players, my staff because when we play for FA Cup, for qualification to the Champions League, and we play for the Premier League, just one thing in my mind is the focus – and that’s to being the team to the highest point. That’s what we’ve done.

“I’m the happiest man on the planet to be in this club, this club is extraordinary.

“Of course in the moment this season is over for us, we want to arrive in the last game to our fans. And I know they will come and in ten seasons they have been really good in many moments and that is what we have to do until the end.”

The result saw City’s title hopes in ruins.

Sports.title: Chelsea 2 Tottenham 1: Spurs’ relegation battle goes down to final day after Enzo Fernandez and Andrey Santos goals
Sports.content:
WE are going the distance.

Tottenham suffering yet another defeat at Stamford Bridge means the dropzone scrap with West Ham extends to the final day.





Enzo Fernandez’s early pearler and an Andrey Santos strike did the damage.

Though a late Richarlison tap-in added some late, faint Spurs hope which ultimately came to nothing, in spite of a bonkers final ten minutes where the desperate visitors chucked everything they could at Chelsea.

It was hard to work out who enjoyed the result more: the gleeful Blues supporters revelling in their rivals’ suffering – or Hammers hardman fan Ross Kemp who was also in attendance here.

Now we are set for a dramatic finale befitting of an Eastenders Christmas special to find out which of these London neighbours will be slinging their hook from the Premier League.

Spurs followers know that misery in Chelsea’s backyard is as certain as death, taxes and a Mitchell brothers barney.

Their barely believable run at Stamford Bridge now stands at: Played 41, won ONE.

And yet they had gone into this clash feeling their luck could actually change for once, given the new life that Roberto De Zerbi has breathed back into their survival bid.

The Italian had presided over a four-game unbeaten streak which, coupled with Nuno Espirito Santo’s Irons losing three on the bounce, meant they needed only a point here to stay up.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

That was due to the two-point gap to 18th-placed West Ham being effectively three because of Spurs’ vastly superior goal difference.

It remains the case heading into Sunday when Tottenham host Everton and the Hammers entertain Leeds.

But it could have been done and dusted from the North Londoners perspective had they not felt that familiar sinking feeling in SW6 last night.

In theory, Chelsea were there for the taking, having lost nine of their last 11, including Saturday’s FA Cup final against Manchester City, and with interim Calum McFarlane still holding the fort.



That is, of course, until the exciting Xabi Alonso takes over in July.

But, as ever, the Blues found a way to lift themselves against their North London neighbours and keep their European qualification pursuit alive.

Though Bournemouth’s point against Manchester City – which gifted Arsenal the title – means the slim chance of Alonso bossing the club in the Champions League next term is now over.

Spurs started pretty well, with Jorrel Hato almost poking a clearance past his own keeper and Mathys Tel crashing a header against the post.

But nothing ever seems to go right for them at this ground – to the point where De Zerbi even addressed the atrocious record with his troops on Tuesday morning – and so it proved again.



With just 18 minutes on the clock, Fernandez suddenly had acres of space outside the Spurs box to let fly from 25 yards.

Keeper Antonin Kinsky got nowhere near the ball which dipped and swerved its way into the near corner.

That sparked a chant of “Tottenham Hotspur, it’s happening again” from the Matthew Harding Stand.

Fernandez almost had a second when he blasted a free-kick onto the crossbar from an acute angle.

First was when Randal Kolo Muani miscued a cross badly out of play, before Mathys Tel got the same treatment for smashing a woeful shot into Row Z.

Spurs were drifting and De Zerbi knew it, so prepared to make a triple substitution including James Maddison in the 67th minute.



But as the trio waited, stripped and ready to come on, Chelsea scored again.

Muani gifted the ball to Cole Palmer, sparking a move which saw Pedro Neto cross for Enzo, who cut it back for Santos to roll into the corner.

It was a hammer blow that looked to have KO’d Spurs chances in this game.



Yet De Zerbi has added a more resilient streak and, with 17 minutes to go, sub Pape Sarr’s backheeled shot squirmed its way to Richarlison who slotted home.

It looked like it would get even better when Maddison was suddenly free deep inside the box, but his close-range shot was blocked by Hato.

From the resulting corner, mayhem ensued as Marc Cucurella wrestled an irate Micky van de Ven to the ground and was booked.

But NO penalty was given because technically the ball was not in play.

The madness continued as Liam Delap appeared to catch Djed Spence in the face with an elbow but escaped with a caution.

This is how SunSport’s Chelsea reporter Lloyd Canfield rated the players…

ROBERT SANCHEZ – 6

With Chelsea eyeing up a keeper in Robin Roefs for the summer, Sanchez has got a point to prove between now and the end of the season, especially with the impending return of Mike Penders from his loan, too.

He kept the Blues in it at 0-0 when he got down low to Tel’s header off the post, but couldn’t do anything to stop Richarlison from getting Spurs back in the game.



Was dependable on the whole.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

JOSH ACHEAMPONG – 5

Tonight was a massive chance for the 19-year-old to impress at right-back, with Malo Gusto out and Reece James on the bench.

He progressed the ball relatively well down the right, and wasn’t caused heaps of problems by Tel and Udogie on the Spurs left, although he was a little slow to get to his man.

WESLEY FOFANA – 5

Wasn’t made to struggle too much by Richarlison on the end of any Spurs crosses going into the middle, and the Frenchman was largely dominant at the back.



He played Richarlison onside as Spurs got a goal back.

JORREL HATO – 7

It’s been a successful season for Hato, with plenty of encouraging signs in the last few games in particular for the youngster.

A nervy loose touch almost put the ball in the back of his own net within the first five minutes, but he soon improved and progressed the ball out nicely from the back.

Is well deserving of a spot in Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea XI next season for my money, and will have a bright future here thanks to his versatility and composure.

Made a massive block to deny Maddison at the death.



MARC CUCURELLA – 5

Was progressing high up the pitch for Chelsea on the left, as he is expected to do under Xabi Alonso if he is still here next season.

He was solid defensively against Kolo Muani, who looked a bag of nerves more often than not on the ball, but it was his poor header out from the back that led to Spurs finding a way back into the game.

ANDREY SANTOS – 8

With Reece James on the bench and Enzo Fernandez higher up, tonight represented a chance for Santos to prove why it was a mistake for Carlo Ancelotti to leave him out of Brazil‘s World Cup squad.

It’s not been the season he will have hoped for when he arrived in the summer, but tonight was one of his better showings, with some strong tackles and an ability to keep things ticking in midfield.



His left-footed stroke into the back of the net capped off a good night for the Brazilian.

MOISES CAICEDO – 6

Caicedo did what he had to do tonight, and did it well.

Nonstop in the Blues midfield, he made life really difficult for Conor Gallagher, and progressed the ball nicely too, never doing too much with it at his feet.

COLE PALMER – 3

It feels like forever since we’ve seen Cole Palmer at his unstoppable best.



Keen for a spot on the plane to the World Cup, and to impress new manager Xabi Alonso, this game was Palmer’s penultimate chance to impress before the summer.

He stroked a shot into the right palm of Kinsky within the first 15 minutes, and failed to do much more than that despite some clever touches.

Needs the summer off, for me.

ENZO FERNANDEZ – 9

His position in this Chelsea team has been one of the most interesting to keep an eye on since Liam Rosenior was sacked, and he flirted with a move to Real Madrid.



His stunning opener from outside the box was too good for Kinsky, and would’ve certainly caught the attention of Xabi Alonso, but his mobile phone celebration would have too…

It would’ve been interesting to see how he celebrated when he rattled the crossbar minutes later from a free-kick.

Turned nothings into somethings for his side, with a neat assist for Andrey Santos too.

PEDRO NETO – 7

The Chelsea winger will take the assist for Fernandez’s goal, but it was a simple pass for the midfielder to do all the work from there.



His involvement in the second won’t earn him any G/A, but it was a brilliantly swept cross into Fernandez, who setup Santos to finish.

He smelled blood on Destiny Udogie after that, and went for him until the end.

LIAM DELAP – 2

One Premier League goal, that is all Chelsea have got out of Liam Delap for £30million this season – his biggest cheer of the night came when he won a foul from Micky Van de Ven.

Not good enough to end Chelsea’s ‘number 9 curse’, and not fit to wear the Chelsea shirt.

Gave Udogie an elbow at the end for good measure and was lucky to stay on the pitch.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

SUBS:

TREVOH CHALOBAH (JOSH ACHEAMPONG, 74) – 5

Didn’t make much of an impact in terms of stability at the back for Chelsea, but didn’t make any errors either.

MAMADOU SARR (WESLEY FOFANA, 81) – 5

It felt like forever since Sarr had played for Chelsea, but he was decent when he came on.

DARIO ESSUGO (COLE PALMER, 88) – N/A

LIAM DELAP (SHIM MHEUKA, 88) – N/A

ALEJANDRO GARNACHO (PEDRO NETO, 88) – N/A

Sports.title: Arsenal stars go wild and dance at training ground as they win Premier League title after watching Man City slip up
Sports.content:
ARSENAL’s stars gathered together at the club’s training ground to celebrate their title win.

The Gunners’ win over Burnley on Monday meant anything but a win for Manchester City the following day would confirm their status as champions.





And Pep Guardiola‘s men could not deliver, falling to a 1-1 draw on the south coast to dash their hopes of any final-day drama.

Mikel Arteta‘s decision to gather his stars at Colney to watch the match paid off as the team celebrated their momentous achievement together.

Declan Rice shared a look into the room, as he uploaded a snap with his team-mates to his Instagram account.

He captioned the post, showing several members of the team posing and grinning: “I told you all.. it’s done.”

Former Chelsea star Alexandre Pato and pop star Jess Glynne were among the stars to congratulate the star in the replies to the post.

Video of the infectious moment the side found out they were champions was soon released, with Arsenal‘s biggest names leaping around in excitement and hugging one another.

Bukayo Saka and Gabriel grabbed each other by the scruff of the neck, while Riccardo Calafiori almost lifted William Saliba off the ground.

Defender Jurrien Timber even shared video of a member of club staff, potentially sporting director Andrea Berta, crowd-surfing on top of the celebrations.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Even members of the team who were not at the venue got involved in the celebrations, as Milly White, partner of Arsenal defender Ben White, shared that she had watched along with other Wags from the team.

She enjoyed the game alongside Martin Odegaard‘s wife Helene Spilling, as well as Kai Havertz‘ wife Sophia Havertz.



While Gabriel emotionally called his wife as he broke down into tears.

Former Gunners star Ian Wright was right among the celebrations with the fans.



The 62-year-old popped a bottle of champagne and was even pictured next to a shocked fan and her BABY as fans of all shapes, sizes and ages took in the energetic scenes.

Eli Junior Kroupi scored midway through the second half to stun Guardiola and Co at the Vitality Stadium.

The Spaniard tried everything as he made four attacking changes in hopes of hunting down two goals to flip the tie.

But he could only manage one, a consolation goal thumped in by Erling Haaland.



It is not the end he would have hoped for if he follows through on his plans to depart the club at the end of the season.



But for his former protege, the momentous occasion feels like just the beginning.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Arsenal fans descended on the Emirates to celebrate their big day, with the revelry spilling out of the pubs of North London and on to the streets.

All the latest on Arsenal’s title win…

It has been a long road for the side, having let a comfortable league lead turn into a gritty scrap with City at the top of the table.

Sports.title: Jurgen Klopp has sent Liverpool clear warning about replacing Mohamed Salah this summer
Sports.content:
Jurgen Klopp has sent Liverpool clear warning about replacing Mohamed Salah this summer

Mohamed Salah is set to leave Liverpool at the end of the season - and former manager Jurgen Klopp has already had his say on replacing the Egyptian

View 3 Images Mohamed Salah is leaving Liverpool this summer (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

Jurgen Klopp feels Liverpool will struggle to find anyone capable of replacing Mohamed Salah and insists the club should not "chase shadows" in an attempt to recreate what he brought. Salah is set to leave Anfield when his contract expires at the end of the season.

‌



The 33-year-old forward has featured 441 times for the Reds, netting 257 goals while also providing 122 assists. He secured legendary status on Merseyside and quickly established himself as a fan favourite after joining in 2017.

‌



There has been widespread speculation regarding who might succeed Salah at Liverpool. Names linked with the role include West Ham's Jarrod Bowen, RB Leipzig's Yan Diomande and Bayern Munich's Michael Olise.

‌



Yet former Liverpool manager Klopp has cautioned that the club will never truly replicate Salah's contribution. Speaking earlier this year after confirmation of Salah's upcoming departure, he explained: "If it is impossible, why should you try? Don't try to chase the shadows. Find a new way and play.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Liverpool confirm Mo Salah plan vs Brentford after departing star's dig at Arne Slot READ MORE :

Jamie Carragher savages 'selfish' Mohamed Salah in brutal Cristiano Ronaldo comparison READ MORE :

"I would not be surprised if he plays another six or seven years. He is an all-time great. This specific kind of player is irreplaceable.

‌



"There will be a void that somebody will fill, but the specific player, Mo Salah? I'm not sure there is even another one existing out there. The numbers he produces as a winger are ridiculous."

Klopp added: "I had to process what it means that Mo goes. I am already looking from the outside, so I texted him what I thought. "I am really happy and proud that I was part of the whole journey. My God, what a player he is."

View 3 Images Klopp believes Salah is irreplaceable (Image: Stu Forster/Getty Images)

‌



Still, the German acknowledged that the Egyptian can be difficult company whenever he is not finding the net. Klopp remarked: "Great team-mate, great guy - but not great company when he's not scoring. Special players are a challenge, but we never lost respect for each other. That is what I really like."

Those words ring particularly true in light of Salah's recent social media comments. Following Liverpool's 4-2 defeat to Aston Villa last week, he appeared to take a fresh swipe at manager Arne Slot, having done so earlier in the season after being dropped from the starting line-up.

"I have witnessed this club go from doubters to believers, and from believers to champions," Salah wrote on Saturday. "It took hard work and I always did everything I could to help the club get there. Nothing makes me prouder than that.

‌



View 3 Images Salah hasn't been a happy bunny this season (Image: Liverpool FC/Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

"Us crumbling to yet another defeat this season was very painful and not what our fans deserve. I want to see Liverpool go back to being the heavy metal attacking team that opponents fear and back to being a team that wins trophies. That is the football I know how to play and that is the identity that needs to be recovered and kept for good.

"It cannot be negotiable and everyone that joins this club should adapt to it. Winning some games here and there is not what Liverpool should be about. All teams win games. Liverpool will always be a club that means a great deal to me and to my family.

Article continues below

"I want to see it succeed for long after I have moved on. As I've always said, qualifying to next season's Champions League is the bare minimum and I will do everything I can to make that happen."

Sports.title: Every 2026 World Cup squad in full as France, Brazil and Portugal submit final lists

One of the jobs that a number still need to complete is to submit their final squad lists to FIFA. Each manager will name a 26-man squad for the tournament, with those final lists needing to be submitted by at least June 1.

Some have chosen to go early with their final squads already having been announced, while others have named only provisional squads. Others in the meantime have named no squad at all - albeit still have time to make their final decisions.

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Mohamed Salah accused of being 'selfish' as agreement reached over star
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Mohamed Salah accused of being 'selfish' as agreement reached over star

The stage is set for Liverpool star Mohamed Salah to make a less-than-ideal exit from the club after copping criticism in light of his latest comments against Arne Slot

View 3 Images Mohamed Salah has been heavily scrutinised for his latest comments that could disrupt Liverpool's end to the season (Image: Getty Images)

Mohamed Salah is at the centre of a fresh storm as Liverpool prepare to wrap up their campaign against Brentford. The Reds are still reeling from a second loss in three Premier League outings and have gone almost a month without a win.

‌



Arne Slot's sophomore season at Anfield has failed to live up to the expectations built by his title-winning debut last year. Much was expected from the club following a spend of more than £400million last summer, only to fall flat in a big way.

‌



Salah could still deliver a parting gift to his club of nine years by helping seal a winning finish in his final game for the club. However, his latest outburst has drawn the ire of some pundits as Mirror Football breaks down Wednesday's Liverpool headlines.

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Carragher labels Salah as 'selfish'

After previously suggesting he's been "thrown under the bus" by Slot in December, Salah has taken aim at his chief once again. The Egyptian came off the bench for only the last 15 minutes or so as Liverpool lost 4-2 away to Aston Villa.

Liverpool confirm Mo Salah plan vs Brentford after departing star's dig at Arne Slot READ MORE :

Wayne Rooney slams 'selfish' Mo Salah and tells Arne Slot to deny him Liverpool farewell READ MORE :

But it was Salah's social media commentary after the game that drew criticism. He started off by calling the latest loss "very painful" before praising Jurgen Klopp's "heavy metal" football, which appeared to be a thinly veiled dig at the current product fans are seeing under Slot.

‌



"I want to see Liverpool go back to being the heavy metal attacking team that opponents fear and back to being a team that wins trophies," he continued. "That is the football I know how to play and that is the identity that needs to be recovered and kept for good. It cannot be negotiable and everyone that joins this club should adapt to it."

Salah went on to say making it back into the Champions League next term is the "bare minimum." But then one can understand why some fans may wonder if Salah is unaware as to how those comments hardly helped in that regard.

View 3 Images Jamie Carragher dubbed Salah "selfish" for airing his frustrations about Arne Slot's playing style publicly (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Jamie Carragher was critical of the club icon following his rant in December after he was dropped for the 3-3 draw against Leeds. And he once again took aim at his fellow Kop legend, suggesting the timing of his "selfish" remarks was woeful given the race for Champions League qualification.

"I'm not surprised," said Carragher on Sky Sports. "I told everybody, 'Something else will come before the end of the season. He'll drop another bomb a little bit like Ronaldo did on the way out of Manchester United.' I thought it may come after the end of the season when he'd moved on, but no.

"Less than two years ago, I called him selfish for doing an interview and I think that rings true again. Liverpool have a really important week. They are still not fully qualified for the Champions League and it should be about Liverpool FC, not Salah FC. It's vital that Liverpool make the Champions League positions, but I'm not surprised and it's not a good look at all."

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Riise joins in Salah criticism

Another member of the 2005 Champions League-winning squad to join in the chorus of criticism was John Arne Riise. The retired left-back piggybacked on Carragher's comments and revealed his frustration that Salah couldn't hide his personal grudge for one more week, at least.

Riise, who didn't play in the Istanbul final 21 years ago, concurred that the departing winger could have held his tongue. However, he assured no-one is bigger than Liverpool, even if Salah appears intent to air his frustrations about the manager.

‌



"It annoys me that Mohamed Salah couldn’t at least wait until the season was finished before saying those things," Riise told Bet Victor Online Casino. "Everyone knows he’s leaving, so why not just keep those opinions to yourself until the end? Or why say them at all?

View 3 Images John Arne Riise is not impressed with Salah's latest outburst criticising his manager (Image: Michael Campanella/Getty Images)

"I’ve read what Wayne Rooney said and what Jamie Carragher said, and honestly, I understand why people are reacting the way they are...I’ve met Mo Salah a few times and I’ve always seen him as a lovely person: smiley, friendly, respectful and someone who looks after people.

‌



"That’s why I can’t really understand these comments. It almost feels like a different person writing them. If it’s a PR team advising him to do these things and make his name bigger than the club, then that’s wrong because Liverpool Football Club will always be bigger than any player. Always."

The Norwegian then commented on Rooney's suggestion that Salah won't start against Brentford in light of his outburst. Many would expect the Anfield icon to be given a send-off as a starter in his last game but Riise believes he'll continue in a bench role.

"To be honest, I agree with Rooney on that point," he continued. "I don’t understand why Arne Slot would allow a player to publicly criticise the team and then still give him a big send-off in the final game.

"Why would the manager reward that behaviour after the things that have been said? I would genuinely be surprised if Mohamed Salah starts the final game."

Sports.title: Premier League ace could become first player to win two European trophies in same season
Sports.content:
Premier League ace could become first player to win two European trophies in same season

The winger could be in line to make history this season

View 2 Images Evann Guessand, now playing for Palace, in action for Aston Villa against his current club earlier on in the season (Image: 2025 Visionhaus)

On-loan Crystal Palace winger Evann Guessand has the chance to become the first player ever to win two European trophies in one season. Guessand, 24, signed for Aston Villa in the summer for £26million from Nice, with Unai Emery's side fending off competition from Palace for the forward's signature.

‌



However, the Ivory Coast international made the loan switch to Selhurst Park in January. He will now bag two winners’ medals if Villa and Palace win the Europa League and Europa Conference League, respectively.

‌



Villa will face German side Freiburg on Wednesday, while Palace travel to Leipzig to face Rayo Vallecano a week later. Guessand featured seven times in the Europa League for Villa during the league phase, netting against Go Ahead Eagles and FC Basel.

‌



While he's spent most of his time at Palace on the treatment table due to a knee injury, he's played five times in the Conference League, scoring against Zrinjski Mostar.

The 24-year-old, while not a household name, could be on the cusp of making history should both English sides prevail. Former Manchester United star Antony almost stole the accolade ahead of Guessand last season, however.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



UEFA fume as TNT make unprecedented Champions League final decision READ MORE :

Ollie Watkins delivers brutal Liverpool truth after running them ragged again READ MORE :

The Brazilian moved to Real Betis on loan from United as both his parent club and the Spanish side reached the finals of the Europa League and Conference League, respectively. The 26-year-old was denied two medals as United and Betis both lost.

Guessand made 13 Premier League appearances for Villa before leaving for the Eagles. Sky Sports have reported that if the winger registers eight goal contributions, it will trigger a clause in his loan deal to make it a permanent move for £28m.

It is also said Palace hold an option to buy Guessand for £28.5m if he fails to record eight goal involvements - and that the player has already agreed a four-year contract if his loan is made permanent.

‌



He has scored twice for Palace, netting in the Premier League and Conference League, while notching an assist. Upon joining Palace in the winter window, Guessand seemed to indicate it was the move he had been waiting for all along.

View 2 Images Guessand moved to Crystal Palace in January (Image: 2026 Sebastian Frej)

“I’m really excited, really excited to be here. I was waiting for this moment for a very long time,” he said. "I’m excited to play with my new team-mates and fight with them, because we have some objectives, some targets, and I think with the quality we have, we can achieve something.

“I've seen a lot of qualities in this team. I've seen them playing. I think my first game in the [Premier] League was against Crystal Palace, and I've seen the quality of this team.

“Every player has this mentality to win, and the manager as well. I spoke with him and the way he plays, the way he gets the best from his players, this is what I really like. I want to improve – I want to get better and better every day – so there are lots of reasons to come here.”

Villa will take on Freiburg in Istanbul, Turkey, on Wednesday night in the Europa League final. It will represent Villa's first chance to win a major European trophy since 1982.

Sports.title: Man Utd news: Michael Carrick set for £50m transfer battle as sacrifice named to complete deal
Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Michael Carrick set for £50m transfer battle as sacrifice named to complete deal

Manchester United have been linked with several players ahead of the summer transfer window

View 2 Images Michael Carrick is set to make several key decisions in the summer transfer window (Image: Mark Cosgrove/News Images/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Manchester United can begin focusing on the summer transfer window as the end of the season approaches. The Red Devils have secured third place in the Premier League and will return to the Champions League next term.

‌



Michael Carrick has been a success as interim manager and is set to be given the job on a permanent basis. The 44-year-old coach has previously admitted to being involved in the club’s discussions ahead of the transfer window.

‌



While replacing Casemiro will be among the team’s top priorities, there are other areas that Carrick may choose to strengthen. United have been linked with an interest in Juventus defender Gleison Bremer, who was recently named in Brazil’s World Cup squad.

‌



Meanwhile, it has been claimed that United will need to sell one of their current players to complete a deal for another transfer target. Here, Mirror Football looks at some of the biggest stories surrounding Old Trafford.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

£50m transfer battle

Italian outlet Gazzetta dello Sport has reported that Juventus star Bremer has attracted interest from United. Michael Carrick’s side are said to be “on his trail”, alongside rivals Liverpool.

‌



Raging Roy Keane rips into Bruno Fernandes and Man Utd stars' behaviour in explosive rant READ MORE :

Ruben Amorim set for shock return to management as replacement for another ex-Man Utd boss READ MORE :

It is claimed that the 29-year-old will “listen to possible offers” in the summer, with the Turin club at risk of missing out on a Champions League place. Gazzetta dello Sport reports that Juventus would consider extending the Brazilian’s contract, which currently runs until 2029 and includes a £50million release clause.

While Bremer is deemed to be happy at Juve, the defender is also said to be “in a hurry” to win major honours as he enters his prime years. The Brazil international has won one Coppa Italia since signing from Torino in 2022.

Bremer will aim to achieve success on the world stage as part of Carlo Ancelotti’s Brazil squad this summer. At club level, the centre-back has made 31 appearances for Luciano Spalletti’s side in all competitions.

‌



View 2 Images Noussair Mazraoui has struggled for regular game time at United (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Man Utd star sacrificed for deal

Sky Sport Deutschland has claimed that United must sell Noussair Mazraoui if the club wish to complete a move for Borussia Dortmund full-back Julian Ryerson. The club are said to be among the sides interested in the Norway international.

Ryserson has registered 15 assists in 31 Bundesliga games this term, which reportedly “has not gone unnoticed” by United. He has two years remaining on his deal and is expected to be priced at around £26m.

Article continues below

The Sky Sport Deutschland report details that United are searching for a right-back to challenge Diogo Dalot but any move for Ryerson will depend on Mazraoui leaving Old Trafford. The United defender arrived from Bayern Munich in 2024 and has made 10 league starts so far this season.

Sports.title: Abandoned 62,000-seater UEFA Cup final stadium looks unrecognisable after being left to rot
Sports.content:
Abandoned 62,000-seater UEFA Cup final stadium looks unrecognisable after being left to rot

A stadium with a greater capacity than Anfield and the Emirates is unrecognisable today

View 4 Images Schalke's iconic Parkstadion in Gelsenkirchen was abandoned for years (Image: Getty)

Schalke’s iconic 62,000-seater stadium once hosted the UEFA Cup final before being left to rot. The first leg of the 1997 UEFA Cup final between Schalke 04 and Inter Milan was held at the Parkstadion in Gelsenkirchen, Germany.

‌



The German side won the opening game 1-0. And few today will remember how they beat Inter on penalties in Italy after drawing 1-1 on aggregate, as we look ahead to Wednesday night’s modern iteration of the same fixture - the Europa League final between Freiburg and Aston Villa.

‌



But unlike Wednesday’s venue, the 42,000-seater Besiktas Park, Parkstadion was a giant of its day. Another big difference is that it is no longer used by Schalke’s first team, having been abandoned by the club after they moved to the glossy Veltins Arena in 2001.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Parkstadion was Schalke’s home between 1973 and 2001. In 1967, Gelsenkirchen’s city council gave the go-ahead to build a large stadium and the first fixture held there was a friendly match between Schalke and Feyenoord.

Five matches were played at Parkstadion during the 1974 World Cup, which West Germany ended up winning. It also hosted two group stage matches in Euro 1998.

‌



Abandoned Euros stadium could be demolished after ex-Champions League club kicked out READ MORE :

In between the two tournaments, Michael Jackson performed there during his Bad World Tour in 1988, while the likes of The Rolling Stones and Pink Floyd also graced it in later years.

However, by the 1990s, it had become increasingly clear the stadium was outdated. Renovations in 1998 took its capacity to 62,004 but issues such as its stands being far from the pitch and a lack of cover remained.

View 4 Images Parkstadion was the home of Schalke from 1973 to 2001 (Image: Getty)

‌

Learn more £4.99 HBO Max Get HBO Max here Product Description Aston Villa have reached the UEFA Europa League final where they face SC Freiburg on May 20 . Fans can watch the game without a TNT Sports subscription by signing up to the HBO Max Basic With Ads plan via Prime Video's HBO Max channel.

Schalke deemed it necessary to move to a new modern ground and construction of the Veltins Arena began at an adjacent site in 1998. The current home of the football club opened its doors three years later.

The last competitive game played at Parkstadion was in May 2001, with 65,000 people attending the game, which ended in a 5-3 win over SpVgg Unterhaching. Schalke fans celebrated wildly as they thought the win had clinched them the title, only for a last-minute Bayern Munich equaliser elsewhere to snatch it away.

‌



View 4 Images The glamorous Veltins Arena opened its doors in 2001 (Image: Getty)

Following the Royal Blues’ departure, Parkstadion was left partly demolished by 2008, leaving it in a state of limbo. Even the jumbotron was donated to a stadium in German town Aue.

For years, aerial shots showed the stands lying in a derelict state compared to its prime. But Schalke later launched a major redevelopment project to transform the area into a high-tech campus for their youth academy.

Article continues below

View 4 Images The old and the new stadium are close (Image: Getty)

Since 2020, it has been somewhat reconstructed, now featuring a heavily scaled-down 2,999-capacity alongside a preserved section of the original concrete terracing and a single, fan-saved floodlight mast.

It reopened its doors for competitive matches in the summer of 2020. Schalke's Under-23 and youth academy teams have been using the historic turf as their official home ground ever since as a nod to the club’s rich history.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: £34million signing snubbed as big summer transfer statement made
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: £34million signing snubbed as big summer transfer statement made

The latest round-up of news from the Emirates Stadium

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta and Arsenal are not resting on their laurels (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA, Getty Images)

It's official – Arsenal are Premier League champions for the first time since 2004. The Gunners secured their first title under Mikel Arteta without even playing on Tuesday night, thanks to Bournemouth's 1-1 draw with Manchester City.

‌



That result means the north Londoners are four points clear at the top and therefore untouchable ahead of Sunday's final round of matches. However, on-pitch success hasn’t stopped Arsenal from making transfer plans for the summer. The Gunners hierarchy invested heavily in the squad last summer, spending over £250million in a club record transfer window.

‌



By bringing in an unprecedented eight players, the 2025/26 campaign has already turned out to be the most successful in the club’s recent history, based on their performance across all four competitions. Manager Mikel Arteta will know that reaching the pinnacle is one thing but staying there is another, meaning he will rely on sporting director Andrea Berta again to get deals across the line.

‌



Berta is understood to be working on several outgoings required to balance the books before bringing in new players. Some of the players Arsenal have reportedly shown an interest in are Julian Alvarez, Mateus Fernandes and Tino Livramento in recent weeks.

Here, Mirror Football brings you two of the biggest transfer stories involving the north Londoners.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Arsenal Premier League champions - special edition on sale now After 22 years of near-misses, heartbreak and drama, the Gooners are once again the best team in the land. Our souvenir edition tells the story of what has been an extraordinary season by Mikel Arteta's men. Order your copy here

Kroenke makes transfer statement

Josh Kroenke, Arsenal’s co-chairman and the son of owner Stan Kroenke, has hinted at another significant transfer window for the club this summer. Kroenke Sports & Entertainment (KSE) have invested heavily into the club throughout Arteta’s tenure.

And the good news for the Gunners faithful is that last year’s record transfer outlay doesn’t appear to have been a one-off, with the Kroenkes keen to push on and ensure they remain competitive across England and Europe.

‌



View 3 Images Arsenal co-chairman Josh Kroenke has addressed the fans (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

Writing in the match-day programme ahead of Arsenal’s game with Burnley, Josh said: "We will give everything we’ve got to win major trophies. And you can rest assured that everyone at the club will continue the hard work to make the coming weeks unforgettable.

"We couldn’t have reached this point without the incredible support and backing you have given us once again, and we know you will create another electric atmosphere here tonight. The connection we feel with our supporters fills us with pride.

‌



"Between us, we are building something very special and, wherever this month of May takes us, there will be no standing still when the season ends."

Fabio Vieira snubbed

View 3 Images Fabio Vieira has enjoyed a productive loan spell with Hamburg (Image: Stuart Franklin/Getty Images)

Hamburg have turned down the opportunity to sign Arsenal flop Fabio Vieira permanently from Arsenal for the time being. The Portuguese playmaker, who signed for the Gunners in 2022 for £34m, joined Hamburg last summer on a season-long loan deal.

‌



Arsenal had hoped their out-of-favour midfielder would leave permanently this summer, given they agreed an option-to-buy clause with the German side when the deal was struck. However, that £19.16m option has been snubbed by Hamburg at the end of his loan spell.

The 25-year-old played a key role in helping the club finish well clear of the relegation zone during their first season back in the top flight, scoring seven goals and notching five assists in the league. It is understood HSV would like to pay under €10m (£8.7m) to land Vieira permanently but that figure is substantially lower than the value of the buy-option, which was hastily negotiated between the clubs on transfer deadline day in September.

However, there is still a chance an agreement could be reached, with Vieira keen on a move to Germany and further talks planned. When asked about the possibility of returning to Hamburg next season, Vieira told reporters: "I have to be open to everything. Let’s see what happens.

Article continues below

"No matter what the future brings, I was very happy here and will be forever grateful to the HSV. The club did everything for me, the support was amazing. I feel the love of the fans and the club. They all love me."

Sports.title: Arsenal crowned Premier League champions
Sports.content:
Arsenal have been crowned Premier League champions for the first time in 22 years.

Following three runners-up finishes, the Gunners have sealed top spot after Manchester City drew 1-1 at Bournemouth on Tuesday night.

Arsenal have topped the table for much of the season, but their title bid looked to have hit shaky ground in April. A 2-1 defeat at Man City seemed to hand the title advantage to Pep Guardiola's side but the Gunners rallied and have held off City to win the league for the first time since the Invincibles in the 2003/04 season.

The title ends a six-year period without a trophy and is Arteta's second major honour as manager at the Emirates Stadium.

Midfielder Declan Rice posted a picture on Instagram with his team-mates with the caption "I told you all.. it's done."

Former Gunners boss Arsene Wenger, who led the team to their last title, in 2004, featured in a celebratory post from the Gunners on their X account.

He said: "You did it. Champions go on when others stop. This is your time. Now, go on and enjoy every moment."

Sports.title: Man City's title bid over as Bournemouth draw sees Arsenal crowned champions
Sports.content:
Manchester City's hopes of winning the Premier League title are over after a 1-1 draw at Bournemouth saw Arsenal crowned champions.

Eli Junior Kroupi's curling first-half effort helped give the Gunners a first Premier League title in 22 years, and despite Erling Haaland's late leveller - it means Pep Guardiola has gone without the league title in back-to-back seasons for the first time in his managerial career.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Eli Junior Kroupi fires Bournemouth in front against Man City!

The result also ensured Bournemouth will be playing European football next season, an achievement secured in head coach Andoni Iraola's final home match in charge before his departure.

With Guardiola expected to leave City after the season, City fans still called for him to stay from the away end. They also sang: "We'll fight to the end" - but Bournemouth made sure that fight will not be carried into Sunday's final day.

City had some half chances in the first half, with Jeremy Doku forcing Djorde Petrovic into a good save early on, but rarely troubled the Cherries.

Player ratings: Bournemouth: Petrovic (8); Smith (7), Hill (8), Senesi (8), Truffert (8); Adams (7), Tavernier (7), Scott (6); Rayan (7), Evanilson (7), Kroupi (8)



Subs: Kluivert (6), Brooks (4), Unal (n/a), Cook (n/a)



Man City: Donnarumma (7); Nunes (6), Khusanov (5), Guehi (6), O’Reilly (6); Rodri (7), Kovacic (6), Bernardo (6); Semenyo (5), Haaland (7), Doku (7)



Subs: Foden (5), Cherki (5), Savinho (5), Marmoush (6)



Player of the Match: Eli Junior Kroupi

At the other end, Evanilson missed a glaring chance from six yards out with the goal gaping - with only the offside flag sparing his blushes.

Then came the first half's big moment as Adrien Truffert broke down the left and cut the ball back to Kroupi, who left Gianluigi Donnarumma rooted to the spot by finding the top corner.

Guardiola needed a response and it nearly came seconds into the second half - but Petrovic managed to deny Nico O'Reilly when the City defender was played through.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nico O'Reilly was denied by Djordje Petrovic as Bournemouth survived a scare early in the second half!

After City brought on Rayan Cherki, Phil Foden and Savinho in an attacking move, Bournemouth got more joy at the other end. Kroupi curled over a good chance from the edge of the box, before Rayan hit the post from close range at a corner.

But despite more City pressure, Bournemouth looked mostly likely to get a second as David Brooks missed two golden chances to seal the game - including hitting the post when clean through.

Haaland equalised in the final minute after Rodri hit the post. But the final whistle sparked jubilant scenes in Dorset and the red half of north London. It looks like all Guardiola has in Sunday's final game with Aston Villa is a farewell bow.

Pep reacts to conceding title - and will he stay?

Image: Pep Guardiola shows his frustration as Manchester City's Premier League hopes end with the draw at Bournemouth

Man City manager Pep Guardiola:

"Expanding on his response over his future in the post-match press conference, Guardiola added: "Listen, with the club, always I talk, but not now.

"The first thing you have to understand is you should talk with my chairman first, right? And after that, when I talk with my chairman, we'll decide.

When asked if the talks will come after their final match of the season on Sunday, Guardiola said: "No, no, we'll talk the next few days.

"Always we talk with my chairman. What are we going to do, what are we not going to do. But I think he [the chairman] deserves [to be the first one spoken to], right?

On whether Sunday's match will be his last at City, he added: "Let me talk about my chairman! I know they [the fans] love me so much. I love them more. I know that it's the best place to be. I love that place [the Etihad]. I adore it.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Manchester City players and Arsenal fans reacted to the Gunners sealing the Premier League title after Man City's 1-1 draw with Bournemouth.

"Let me talk about my club. Even though people say I talk to a thousand million people in person, I was incredibly, incredibly focused on my job. When we are in the competitions, I'm there. I was there. This is what I have to do."

Iraola: I'm not sure where I will go

Bournemouth head coach Andoni Iraola to Sky Sports:

"At the beginning of the season you didn't imagine [Europe]. It has been so nice and we have a chance to fight for the Champions League in the last game and we really deserve this, especially for the game we played so well. We have not won the game but it does not matter.

"Today has been a good reflection of the club. I'm very happy for the club, the players, the supporters and the staff. It's the best way to finish with something you can touch I can't ask for anything more.

"Pep is the top of the top. He has won everything. It was a difficult game for them, they played three days ago with the tension of a final. We made them play a difficult game and they were obviously tired but they have this quality. It makes it even more nice when you play like this against an opposition that are so good.

"We have a special group of players. They are consistent and always there. Right now there is nothing about my future in my head, I just want to celebrate and push it. We have Europa League, next let's maximise our options. Can we take the last Champions League spot?

"I still don't know where I will go but I'm in no rush, let's finish on a high."

Richards: Guardiola the greatest manager of his generation

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Following the 1-1 draw with Bournemouth in the Premier League, Manchester City boss Pep Guardiola remained coy on his future at the club and told Sky Sports that he will talk to the chairman at the end of the season.

Former Man City defender Micah Richards on Sky Sports:

"He is the greatest manager of his generation without doubt and I say that because of the way he plays football. There are certain ways you can win a football match.

"Arteta and Arsenal have done it a little bit more defensively. But in terms of his 10-year tenure at Man City, whether it's full-backs inverted, false nines, playing (John) Stones in central midfield in the Champions League final, he has just created a way to love the game and for the game to be played in the right way."
